gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.description: Every feature is configured with a custom resource. This portal shows the live status of those resources; it refreshes every 15 seconds.

nodeLifecycleRules.subtitle: Cordon and drain nodes before the cloud provider removes them
nodeLifecycleRules.description: A NodeLifecycleRule reads node lifecycle notifications from a queue (EC2 Spot interruption warnings or Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks), finds the node whose providerID matches the instance and drains it gracefully.

features.f1: Cluster-scoped rule with pluggable queue providers (aws-sqs today).
features.f2: The message is acknowledged before draining, so the controller can safely drain its own node.
features.f3: Configurable drain timeout, grace period, DaemonSet and emptyDir handling, and optional node selector.
features.f4: Several nodes are drained in parallel within the provider's notice window.

queueTriggeredJobs.subtitle: Launch Kubernetes Jobs when a queue has pending work
queueTriggeredJobs.description: A QueueTriggeredJob polls a queue and creates a Job from a CronJob template (or an inline template) once the approximate depth reaches minMessages, without exceeding maxActiveJobs.

features.f1: Scale batch workers to zero when the queue is empty.
features.f2: Jobs are owned by the resource and garbage-collected with ttlSecondsAfterFinished.
features.f3: Jobs started by the referenced CronJob count towards the concurrency limit.
features.f4: Run a Job on demand from this portal or POST /api/v1/.../run.

alertRemediations.subtitle: Self-healing actions triggered by Alertmanager
alertRemediations.description: An AlertRemediation matches Alertmanager webhook alerts by name, labels and an optional numeric threshold, then deletes the affected pod or performs a rolling restart of its workload.

features.f1: Only pods in the AlertRemediation's own namespace can be acted upon.
features.f2: Thresholds accept plain numbers or percentages ("50%").
features.f4: Actions: DeletePod or RolloutRestart (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet).

postDeployTests.subtitle: Run tests after every deployment
postDeployTests.description: A PostDeployTest reacts to Flux notification events and starts an in-cluster Job and/or an external CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or Bitbucket Pipelines).

features.f1: Match Flux events by kind, name, namespace, reason and message.
features.f2: Pipeline credentials are read from a Secret in the same namespace.
features.f3: Cooldown avoids duplicate runs when Flux emits several events.
features.f4: Run tests on demand from this portal or the API.
